newsitem.title: USA: Chiron unit applies with FDA for license.
newsitem.headline: Chiron unit applies with FDA for license.

text.p: Chiron Corp unit Chiron Vaccines said Tuesday it filed for a product license from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration covering a vaccine used to fight diptheria, tetanus and genetically engineered acellular pertussis (DTaP) in children.

The vaccine, called Pertugen, is one of a new generation of vaccines that would make childhood immunization safer, Pertugen is the first DTaP vaccine derived from recombinant DNA technology to detoxify the pertussis toxin. Pertussis is also known as "whooping cough."
In clinical trials, immunization of infants with Pertugen was highly protective against pertussis and was connected to fewer possibly serious side effects than currently used whole-cell DTP vaccines.
Chiron shares were up 1/4 to 19-1/4 following the news.
